top_story.headline: Quiet window: no new FEC correspondence beyond what earlier editions reported
top_story.dek: Every Form 99 and request for additional information (RFAI) indexed since October 4 was already covered in a prior edition.
paragraphs: The FEC filings feed returned 148 Form 99 and RFAI records received October 4–6, and all of them were already reported in earlier editions, so none are repeated here.

The one new item is a $20,000 candidate-loan reversal at Lily 4 Congress Committee, in the Voided & Negative Transactions section below. A keyword scan of RFAI filings for fraud-related terms turned up only the FEC's standard boilerplate warning about false statements, not any allegation against a committee.

sections.headline: One Candidate Loan to Campaign Reversed
paragraphs: One large negative amount was reported this week. In FEC filings, negative transaction amounts represent voided, reversed, or refunded contributions—typically routine bookkeeping corrections, but occasionally the paper trail for something being unwound after the fact.

items: Lily 4 Congress Committee reversed a $20,000 loan from Lily Tang Williams, dated December 31, 2025 (reported October 5, 2026). The filing describes this as "loans received from the candidate" being reversed. View filing.

sections.headline: No new RFAIs or Form 99s this window
paragraphs: All 76 RFAI (FRQ) and 72 Form 99 records received since October 4 were already reported in prior editions; nothing new to list.
